title: Reduction commutes with completed pullback
statement:
Let $g:T'\to T$ be a morphism of schemes and use the Noetherian adic datum $A,I,P_n=A/I^n$, coefficient sheaves $A_W=\varprojlim_n(P_n)_W$ for $W=T,T'$, and reduction tower of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. Let $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(T_{\Proet},A_T))$ be derived $I$-complete in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion], and put $K_n=K\otimes^L_{A_T}(P_n)_T$. Let $L=Lg^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(T'_{\Proet},A_{T'}))$ be the completed pullback of [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], and write $g_n^*$ for finite-coefficient module pullback as there.

Then $L$ is derived $I$-complete, and for every $n\geq1$ the projection of its defining derived limit to $Lg_n^*K_n$ induces a functorial isomorphism in $D(\operatorname{Mod}(T'_{\Proet},(P_n)_{T'}))$,
$$\alpha_n:L\otimes^L_{A_{T'}}(P_n)_{T'}\xrightarrow{\sim}Lg_n^*K_n.$$
These isomorphisms commute with the quotient transition maps. For $b\geq a\geq1$ they also commute with normalization: extending $\alpha_b$ from $(P_b)_{T'}$ to $(P_a)_{T'}$ and then using the normalization of the pulled-back reduction tower gives $\alpha_a$ after the canonical scalar-extension associativity identification. For $c\geq b\geq a$ these normalizations satisfy the quotient cocycle, and for equal indices the unit identity. All tensor products in the display are over the indicated sheaves of rings; no identification with an ordinary module derived category is asserted.

proof.text: Write $\underline A_W$ for the constant coefficient ring on $W_{\Proet}$, and $\operatorname{Res}_W$ for restriction from $A_W$ to $\underline A_W$. Set $N=Lg^*_{\underline A}\operatorname{Res}_T K$, in the constant-coefficient derived category on $T'$. By [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] and [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], restriction of the defining pulled-back strict tower identifies it with the strict reduction tower $N_n=N\otimes^L_{\underline A_{T'}}\underline{P_n}_{T'}$, and identifies its derived limit $\operatorname{Res}_{T'}L$ with $\widehat N=R\lim_nN_n$, respecting the completion unit $\eta:N\to\widehat N$ and all finite projections. The finite comparison is the canonical one to $Lg_n^*K_n$. These are comparisons of strict towers and their derived limits, not an exchange of pullback with an infinite limit. The coefficient hypotheses of [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum] hold here: take $\Lambda=A$ on $T'$, with the same ideal and perfect quotients as in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum].

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case, clause (5), and Tag 099M, lemma-naive-completion; coefficient comparison as in the completed-pullback definition

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-koszul-completion-reflector] on the small site $T'_{\Proet}$ with $\mathcal O=\underline A_{T'}$ and the finite generators of $I$. Its Koszul derived limit is locally derived $I$-complete for any input $N$; no completeness of ordinary pullback is needed. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], this Koszul limit is $\widehat N$, with the same unit. That node identifies restriction of the completed-coefficient quotient limit with this constant-coefficient limit and identifies Koszul completeness with local completeness. Therefore $L$ is derived $I$-complete in precisely the intrinsic sense of [def-weil-pbc-intrinsic-completion]. More explicitly, apply the same reflector with $\mathcal O=A_{T'}$ to $L$. Restriction identifies its Koszul unit with the Koszul unit of $\operatorname{Res}_{T'}L=\widehat N$: termwise tensor with the finite free Koszul factors commutes with restriction, and the derived-limit comparison is the one in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. The latter unit is an isomorphism by the constant-coefficient reflector. Restriction is exact and does not change underlying abelian sheaves, so a cone becomes acyclic under restriction only if it was already acyclic. It therefore reflects isomorphisms, and the Koszul unit of $L$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 099B and 0A0E, lemma-derived-completion and lemma-derived-completion-koszul; proetale.tex Tag 099M

proof.text: Put $R=\underline A_{T'}$ and $S_a=\underline{P_a}_{T'}$. The coefficient datum gives a bounded finite-projective $A$-complex representing $P_a$; taking constant sheaves gives a global strict-perfect package [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Realize strict towers as modules on the site $\mathcal C\times\mathbf N_{\geq1}$, with arrows $(U,n)\to(V,m)$ for $n\leq m$ induced by arrows $U\to V$, and coverings at a fixed index induced by coverings of $\mathcal C=T'_{\Proet}$. A sheaf there is exactly an inverse sequence of sheaves on $\mathcal C$. Give it the ring sheaf $\Delta R$. The projection defines a ringed-topos morphism $h$ with $h^{-1}=\Delta$, $h_*=\lim$, and identity coefficient map. Thus its total derived direct image is the strict $R\lim$ of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], while $Lh^*F=\Delta F$ since constant towers are exact. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-totalization] to this $h$, the Koszul tower of $N$, and the global package $F$ representing $S_a$, using the arrows of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows]. It gives the canonical isomorphism $(R\lim X_m)\otimes_R^L F\to R\lim(X_m\otimes_R^L F)$. The ordinary representative specified in that definition is $x\otimes f\mapsto(x_m\otimes f)_m$ on a tower K-injective resolution. Evaluation at $m$ therefore gives projection tensored with $1_F$. Likewise, for a strict compatible family $M\to X_m$, its composite sends $z\otimes f$ to the family of the images of $z$ tensored with $f$. These equalities of chain maps prove compatibility with evaluation and with the map induced from a constant tower, including the Koszul unit. The unit-preserving Koszul/quotient comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] identifies its left side with $\widehat N\otimes_R^L S_a$ and its reduced unit with $r_a=\eta\otimes^L1$. Thus it remains to compute $R\lim_m(N\otimes_R^L Q_m(R)\otimes_R^L S_a)$ and this reduced unit. Use one K-flat representative $C$ of $N$ [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. Since $Q_m(R)$ is bounded finite free, the tensor is represented by $C\otimes_R(Q_m(R)\otimes_R S_a)$. For $m\geq a$, every $a_j^m$ vanishes in $P_a$, so the Koszul differential is zero. Its degree-zero summand gives the constant tower $C\otimes_R S_a$, and its negative-degree summands, indexed by nonempty subsets $J$ of the generators, have transition $m+a\to m$ equal to multiplication by $\prod_{j\in J}a_j^a=0$. This is an equality of chain maps, even though $C$ is unbounded. The reduced unit is the inclusion into the degree-zero summand. The cone tower of that inclusion has zero transitions over a gap of $a$ on the tail. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] its derived limit is zero, hence the inclusion induces an isomorphism on derived limits. Discarding the finitely many indices $m<a$ has no effect: extend the tail constantly at its first term to the earlier indices and map that tower into the original one by the original transitions; its cone tower is eventually zero, so the same theorem gives an isomorphism on derived limits. The constant tower has derived limit $C\otimes_R S_a$: in the product triangle, the map from the product to $(C\otimes_R S_a)\oplus\prod_n^D(C\otimes_R S_a)$ with components first projection and $1-s$ is an isomorphism. Its inverse sends $(z,(y_n))$ to $(z,z-y_1,z-y_1-y_2,\ldots)$; each component uses only a finite sum. Under this isomorphism $1-s$ is the second projection, whose split triangle has first term $C\otimes_R S_a$ embedded diagonally. This also identifies its canonical unit as the identity. It follows that $r_a:N_a\to\widehat N\otimes_R^L S_a$ is an isomorphism. Using the canonical derived adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows] for the identity underlying topos with ring map $R\to S_a$ (direct image is exact restriction of scalars), define $\beta_a$ to be the scalar-extension adjoint of the level-$a$ projection $\widehat N\to\operatorname{Res}N_a$. Step 4 will identify it with $r_a^{-1}$. The finite-reduction and evaluation comparisons of [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] and [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] then identify $\beta_a$ with the asserted projection-induced $\alpha_a$. No theorem about an arbitrary tower recovering its levels is used.

source.place: Proof, Koszul reduction and pro-zero negative-degree calculation, with explicit quotient-tower hypotheses from step 1; tensor/limit exchange specializes order 1267 (lemma-weil-pbc-projection-formula-totalization) to the tower site of Stacks Tag 0940 (section-derived-limits), using Tag 0944 (lemma-projection-formula).

proof.text: In constant coefficients put $r_a=\eta\otimes^L1:N_a\to\widehat N\otimes^L\underline{P_a}_{T'}$ and denote the projection-induced map of step 3 by $\beta_a$. Then $\beta_a r_a=1_{N_a}$: write $p_a:\widehat N\to\operatorname{Res}N_a$ for the projection and $u_a:N\to\operatorname{Res}N_a$ for the quotient unit. The projection-induced map $\beta_a$ is the scalar-extension adjoint of $p_a$, and $p_a\eta=u_a$. Consequently $\beta_a(\eta\otimes^L1)$ is the scalar-extension adjoint of $u_a$, namely $1_{N_a}$, by the unit identity of the canonical derived adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-projection-formula-arrows], applied to the identity underlying topos with ring map $R\to S_a$; its direct image is exact restriction of scalars and its derived pullback is extension of scalars. On a K-flat model its composite sends $x\otimes s$ to $(x\otimes1)s=x\otimes s$. The unit/projection compatibility needed here is in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence]. Since $r_a$ is an isomorphism by step 3, this identity proves $\beta_a=r_a^{-1}$ and hence proves that $\beta_a$ and its completed-coefficient counterpart $\alpha_a$ are isomorphisms. Thus these isomorphisms and their inverses are natural in $K$: the finite comparisons and unit are natural, and inversion preserves a natural commuting square.

source.place: Detailed form, functoriality; the projection-induced reduction map is the inverse of the reduced completion unit

proof.text: For $b\geq a$, naturality of tensoring the single map $\eta$ with the quotient $P_b\to P_a$ gives $\widehat q_{b,a}r_b=r_aq_{b,a}$. Substituting $r_j=\beta_j^{-1}$ and composing with the inverses gives $q_{b,a}\beta_b=\beta_a\widehat q_{b,a}$, proving transition compatibility. For normalization, write $\theta^N_{b,a}$ and $\theta^{\widehat N}_{b,a}$ for the scalar-extension associativity maps of [def-weil-pbc-complete-coefficient-datum]. Its naturality gives $\theta^{\widehat N}_{b,a}(r_b\otimes^L1)=r_a\theta^N_{b,a}$. Cancel the isomorphisms $r_a$ and $r_b\otimes^L1$ to obtain $\theta^N_{b,a}(\beta_b\otimes^L1)=\beta_a\theta^{\widehat N}_{b,a}$. The normalization cocycle and unit law are those of the same coefficient-datum node: both three-level composites send $((x\otimes t)\otimes s)\otimes v$ to $x\otimes q_{c,a}(t)q_{b,a}(s)v$. Finally the natural finite comparisons in [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence] identify these equations with the equations for $\alpha$ and the pulled-back tower; the completed-pullback definition identifies that tower including its transitions. This proves all stated compatibilities.

blueprint_sketch.proof:
Derived pullback commutes with derived tensor, so its defining tower is the
reduction tower of $Lg^*K$. Apply finite reduction of adic completion to
this object. Its level $n$ is
$Lg^*K\otimes^L_\Lambda P_n\simeq Lg^*(K\otimes^L_\Lambda P_n)=Lg^*K_n$.
